report:
Finding: No finetuning effect is detectable; Model B is effectively identical to Model A on the measured axes. The finetuning objective appears to be “none” (or the measurement captured no change).

Reasoning:
- Difference norms are exactly 0 at every layer and token position. This implies the residual-stream activation difference (B − A) is the zero vector everywhere we measured, so there’s no concentrated signal to interpret.
- The logit-lens readouts are the same across all cells and consist of generic, high-frequency tokens (“ o”, “is”, “it”, etc.), which is what you’d expect when projecting a near-zero/noisy vector into vocab space—no meaningful directional signal.
- Patchscope readouts are empty; injecting a zero difference into an identity prompt yields no change, consistent with no detectable difference.

Conclusion: Either
- No finetune was applied (Model B = Model A), or
- The instrumentation/run failed to capture any change, or
- Any finetune effect lies outside the probed positions/components.

Given the evidence, the most plausible report is that there is no observable finetuning objective.
